title: V8 Cube stage: two drain modes side by side
formula: score = Q @ K^T and pv = P @ V over HiFloat8 operands decoded to FP32, 128x128 tiles
study_for: The controlled side-by-side of `dual_mode`: one `l0c_qk` tile is drained twice — `SPLITN` into a per-sub-block `ub_score[TILE, 64]`, then `SINGLE` into the whole `ub_full[TILE, TILE]` that only sub-block 0 stores — and both are published to GM so the reference can compare them. `score2` is the two 64-query halves concatenated; `score3` is the complete tile. Read this before choosing a drain mode anywhere.

A mutex's pipes belong to the CONSUMER, not to a convention. Both bridges here are consumed by MTE3 stores rather than by V-pipe `@vf` bodies, so `dst_start_pipe`/`dst_end_pipe` are MTE3. Put V there and the free fires while the store is still reading the tile; `--launcher pipesim` reports that as a WAR hazard.

Physical NZ padding is not part of the answer. The 33-row fractal stride makes row 33 of each fractal padding, and the reference excludes it from the decoded live P matrix. `padding_poison` fills that row with 0xA5 and the result must not move by one bit — which it does not, so a reader of that row would be caught immediately.
The reference builds every HiFloat8 value from exponent/fraction classes instead of calling the execution codec. A reference that used the codec it is checking would agree with a codec defect.
do_not_copy_when: You want a complete attention kernel. This is a stage diagnostic — QK, one drain of each mode, and a PV — with no online softmax state and no tail handling.
Your operands are not HiFloat8 in the NZ physical layout. The packing, the 33-row stride and the decode are half of what this demo is showing.
